text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. By studying these patterns, they learn to predict the next word in a sentence, which lets them generate human-like responses. To get a useful answer, users must practice prompt engineering—that is, writing clear, specific questions or instructions. LLMs can write essays, summarize information, and even help with coding, but they have limits. They sometimes produce incorrect or outdated facts, and they don't truly understand meaning like people do. They are powerful tools, but they work best when we check their output carefully.
